measurement.mode: static Vite client bundle graph — no browser, no network, no rendering
measurement.browser: not applicable. The gate never launches a browser; it reads the chunk graph the Vite build emits (dist/client/bundle-graph.json) and sums, per route, the client entry chunk, the static-import closure of the route's own chunk, and the chunks of its layout ancestors (a nested route renders its parent layouts). Browser-dependent behaviour is out of scope by design — see Issue #384 (Lighthouse measurement) and #385 (score gate).
measurement.network: not applicable. Budgeted numbers are RAW on-disk bytes of the files a browser must fetch before the route is interactive. gzip -9 figures are printed for reference only and are never budgeted, because a CDN's compression settings are not part of this measurement.
measurement.cpu: not time-based. The measurement is byte arithmetic over a build artefact, so it is deterministic on any machine and independent of runner speed. Only the wall-clock cost of `pnpm run build` that produces the artefact is runner-dependent.
measurement.source_sha: the commit the run is executed at, printed as `git rev-parse HEAD`. In CI the client build and this check run in the same job against the same SHA, so a red run always names the exact tree that was measured; locally, rebuild before rerunning if the tree changed. The gate also warns (it does not fail) when the graph's recorded client assets no longer exist under its own out_dir, which is what a stale or foreign `dist/client/bundle-graph.json` looks like.
measurement.reproduce_locally: pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check
measurement.reproduce_in_ci: the `validate` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `pnpm run validate:integration`, which runs this check immediately after `pnpm run build:production`.

headroom_policy: Every JS cap is the measured `initial_js_bytes` plus at least 0.35% headroom, rounded up to the next multiple of 5,000 bytes: `ceil(measured * 1.0035 / 5000) * 5000`. The current caps were re-derived from one `pnpm run build` of this branch measured at `2793bd80` (the PR head at the time of the measurement). `origin/release-0-7-0` stood at `38c28818` then, and its newer commits touch only `src/http/**` and `src/server.ts` — server-side code that is not part of the client bundle graph — so the measurement describes the tree CI builds as well. Measured initial JS on that build ranged from 1,587,977 B (`/admin`) to 1,637,331 B (`/design-system`), and the slack the formula leaves is +0.39% (`/admin/keys`) to +0.64% (`/admin/emoji-catalog`). The initial CSS measured 42,397 B, inside the shared 45,000 B cap. CSS is budgeted on one shared cap rather than per route: the initial stylesheet is a single asset every route pulls in, so a per-route CSS cap would be 16 copies of the same number. That shared CSS cap was re-derived after the base merged #485 (`src/styles.css` font first-paint work), which moved the measured initial CSS from 38,681 B to 40,028 B; the cap is 45,000 B for the same reason JS caps are rounded to 5,000 B boundaries (one boundary of headroom on a number that is already inside it). Measured bytes are read back from the files Rollup emitted (`writeBundle` in `vite.config.ts` → `scripts/_client-bundle-graph.mjs`), so a cap is compared against the exact bytes a browser downloads — including the preload marker and dependency map that Vite injects after an ordinary user plugin's `generateBundle` runs. Because the entry shell is shared, ~1.5 MiB of every admin route, a base merge that adds a few hundred bytes to the shell re-derives several route caps at once; that is why a release merge turns this gate red until the caps are re-measured with `pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check`. It is the gate doing its job, not a flaky test. The caps are intentionally tight: the entry chunk alone is ~1.5 MiB because `emoji-picker-react` is statically imported (see the Vite chunk warning in the build log), so a per-route cap is the only place a regression of that kind is visible today. Reducing the shell is a separate change with its own Issue; this gate only makes the number visible and stops it from moving silently. Note that raising a cap is not machine-checked — only an `exception` is — so a cap change is expected to carry its measurement and rationale in the PR diff. Issue #496 re-derived every route cap twice: the published data-lifecycle registry (`src/privacy/data-lifecycle.ts`) ships to the client through the home footer, so the shared entry shell grew by 10.7 KiB of static bilingual policy text, and the review round grew it a little further (the analytics sentence now names the first-page_view limit, and the admin-auth sentence names the token-gated accept page). `/admin` measured 1,587,977 B, and the five routes whose measured bytes crossed their previous cap boundary (`/admin/`, `/admin/emoji-catalog`, `/admin/invitations/accept`, `/contact`, `/portfolio/$slug`) moved up by one 5,000 B step each; the other eleven caps did not move. The shared CSS cap (measured 42,397 B) and the Tool iframe aggregate were not touched. A future PR that renders this notice without shipping it — a server-only projection — should re-derive the caps downward again. A JS cap is the measured `initial_js_bytes` plus at least 0.35% headroom, rounded up to the next multiple of 5,000 bytes: `ceil(measured * 1.0035 / 5000) * 5000`. A cap records the measurement it was derived from, so a route whose measurement moved after the cap was set can carry a cap that is no longer the formula output — those are named explicitly below and are left alone on purpose, because raising a cap that is not red is a decision, not a measurement. The caps were last re-derived from one `pnpm run build` of this branch with `origin/release-0-7-0` at `b25b0459` merged in, so the numbers describe the tree this PR merges into — not the tree the first draft was written against. Most caps were already re-derived by the release branch; this reconcile re-derived the two the release merge moved: `/design-system` measured 1,620,334 B and `/portfolio/` measured 1,610,859 B, so the caps became 1,630,000 B and 1,620,000 B by the formula below. Observed slack on that build is +0.36% (`/admin`) to +0.67% (`/portfolio/$slug`) for initial JS. The initial CSS measured 40,451 B on that build, still inside the shared 45,000 B cap. CSS is budgeted on one shared cap rather than per route: the initial stylesheet is a single asset every route pulls in, so a per-route CSS cap would be 16 copies of the same number. That shared CSS cap was re-derived after the base merged #485 (`src/styles.css` font first-paint work), which moved the measured initial CSS from 38,681 B to 40,028 B; the cap is 45,000 B for the same reason JS caps are rounded to 5,000 B boundaries (one boundary of headroom on a number that is already inside it). Measured bytes are read back from the files Rollup emitted (`writeBundle` in `vite.config.ts` → `scripts/_client-bundle-graph.mjs`), so a cap is compared against the exact bytes a browser downloads — including the preload marker and dependency map that Vite injects after an ordinary user plugin's `generateBundle` runs. Because the entry shell is shared, ~1.5 MiB of every admin route, a base merge that adds a few hundred bytes to the shell re-derives several route caps at once; that is why a release merge turns this gate red until the caps are re-measured with `pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check`. It is the gate doing its job, not a flaky test. The caps are intentionally tight: the entry chunk alone is ~1.48 MiB because `emoji-picker-react` is statically imported (see the Vite chunk warning in the build log), so a per-route cap is the only place a regression of that kind is visible today. Reducing the shell is a separate change with its own Issue; this gate only makes the number visible and stops it from moving silently.  Issue #498 re-derived three caps the same way: the embed consent gate (`src/tools/embed-privacy.ts` plus its route) adds ~3.6 KB to the shared entry chunk, because the `/tools/<slug>` loader evaluates the third-party contract and TanStack Start keeps loader code in the client bundle for client-side navigation. Measured on this branch (`pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check`): `/admin/invitations/accept` 1,582,353 B, `/portfolio/$slug` 1,616,507 B, `/tools/$slug` 1,582,073 B — so the formula gives 1,590,000 / 1,625,000 / 1,590,000, and those are the caps. Every other cap was left untouched, including `/admin` (1,574,539 B measured, cap 1,575,000 B): raising a cap that is not red would be a decision, not a measurement. The delta was shrunk before the caps were moved — the violation messages and the manifest `basis` strings were cut from 4,099 B to ~3.6 KB of shell growth — because a gate that needs raising is a cheaper outcome than a gate that needs moving. Note that raising a cap is not machine-checked — only an `exception` is — so a cap change is expected to carry its measurement and rationale in the PR diff.

tool_iframe.reason: Each Tool is an independent Vite build loaded inside a sandboxed iframe from /tools/<slug>/app/, so its bytes are never part of a host route's first paint. Capping it separately keeps one heavy Tool from being hidden by the host route budget and stops a Tool from inflating the host measurement. The cap is the observed `prototype` bundle (1,502,757 B JS / 8,415 B CSS) plus headroom; the Tool's own repository owns any reduction.
